title: Request simulator: who acts, what it touches, what it costs and who can stop it
notes: Each step's facts come from the page in its source field, checked on the asOf date. The app decides which steps apply to a request; rates and wording live here so a price change is a data edit. Facets can be a string or an object keyed by variant (licensed, unlicensed, external, user, sp, web, default).

who.label: Employee with Microsoft 365 Copilot
who.phrase: An employee with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license

who.label: Employee without a Copilot license
who.phrase: An employee without a Copilot license

where.label: Copilot Studio agent in Teams or Copilot
where.phrase: asks a Copilot Studio agent in Teams or Copilot

where.label: Copilot Studio agent on a website
where.phrase: asks a Copilot Studio agent on a public website

where.label: Autonomous agent (event-triggered)
where.phrase: An event triggers an autonomous Copilot Studio agent

presets.label: Same agent, unlicensed users
presets.hint: Answers that are free for licensed users become metered

presets.label: One shared service principal
presets.hint: Everyone gets the same rows, and no free allowance

presets.label: Autonomous in a licensed tenant
presets.hint: No user is chatting, so the license doesn't cover it

presets.label: Genie for frontline staff
presets.hint: No Copilot license, still per-user governance

presets.label: Fabric agent behind Copilot Studio
presets.hint: A channel limit that's easy to miss

presets.label: External customer, governed data
presets.hint: No tenant identity, so a service principal it is

entry-copilot-licensed.title: Signs in to Microsoft 365 Copilot
entry-copilot-licensed.identity: The employee's own Entra ID account.
entry-copilot-licensed.access: Enterprise Data Protection covers the prompt and the response, and they aren't used to train foundation models.
entry-copilot-licensed.cost: Covered by the $30 Microsoft 365 Copilot seat for everyday AI. Advanced AI, such as Cowork, is metered separately.
entry-copilot-licensed.control: Microsoft 365 admin center (seats and Copilot settings) and Entra (sign-in and Conditional Access).
entry-copilot-licensed.logs: Purview audit records the Copilot interaction, and prompts and responses are kept for eDiscovery.

entry-copilot-basic.title: Signs in to Copilot Chat without a Copilot license
entry-copilot-basic.identity: The employee's own Entra ID account.
entry-copilot-basic.access: Grounded on the web, not on Microsoft Graph. Work content gets in only by upload, by open documents in Teams or Outlook, or through a pay-as-you-go agent.
entry-copilot-basic.cost: No seat cost. Pay-as-you-go agents are metered in Copilot Credits, and they stay off until an admin sets up billing.
entry-copilot-basic.control: Microsoft 365 admin center: the pay-as-you-go billing policy and which agents these users can use.
entry-copilot-basic.logs: Purview audit records the Copilot interaction.

entry-teams.title: Opens a Teams app
entry-teams.identity: The employee's own Entra ID account. The app acts for them.
entry-teams.access: Admins have to approve the app's permissions and install it before anyone can use it.
entry-teams.cost: Using a Teams app needs no Copilot license.
entry-teams.control: Entra (admin consent for the app) and the Microsoft 365 admin who installs it.
entry-teams.logs: Each platform behind the app logs its own part, as the next step shows.

entry-studio.title: Chats with a Copilot Studio agent in Teams or Copilot
entry-studio.identity: The employee's Entra ID, through 'Authenticate with Microsoft', the default for new agents.
entry-studio.access: Knowledge from SharePoint, Dataverse and Copilot connectors is trimmed to what this user can open. Files uploaded into the agent aren't.

cost.licensed: Included: the agent runs in a Microsoft channel under a licensed user's identity, so its answers, actions and grounding aren't charged (fair use applies).
cost.default: Metered in Copilot Credits: every answer, action and grounding call, because this user has no Copilot license.

entry-studio.control: Power Platform admin center: environments, data policies, billing policies and capacity.
entry-studio.logs: Purview audit records Copilot Studio maker activity.

entry-website.title: Chats with a Copilot Studio agent on a public website

identity.external: No identity in your tenant. With 'No authentication', anyone who has the link can chat.
identity.default: Whatever sign-in the website offers. 'Authenticate with Microsoft' works in Teams, Power Apps and Microsoft Copilot, not on a website.

entry-website.access: Per-user permissions can't help here, so the agent should reach only content that every visitor may see.
entry-website.cost: Always metered. A website isn't a Microsoft channel, so even licensed employees are billed.
entry-website.control: Power Platform admin center: data policies can block 'No authentication' agents and limit channels.
watch: 'No authentication' combined with internal knowledge is the main oversharing risk in Copilot Studio.

entry-cowork.title: Starts a Copilot Cowork task
entry-cowork.identity: The employee's Entra ID. Cowork plans and runs the steps on their behalf.
entry-cowork.access: Works with the same Microsoft 365 permissions the user has.
entry-cowork.cost: Needs the Copilot license plus usage-based billing. Each task consumes Copilot Credits; Microsoft's planning range is 100 to 300 for light tasks, 300 to 700 for medium and 700+ for heavy.
entry-cowork.control: Microsoft 365 admin center spending policies decide who can use Cowork and set budgets. 'Auto-apply new services' is on by default.
entry-cowork.logs: Copilot Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center reports credit usage.

entry-autonomous.title: An event starts an autonomous Copilot Studio agent
entry-autonomous.identity: No person is chatting. The agent acts through the credentials stored in its connections.
entry-autonomous.access: Per-user permissions don't apply: the agent can reach whatever its connections can.
entry-autonomous.cost: Always metered, even if every employee has a Copilot license. The license covers licensed users interacting with an agent, and nobody is.
entry-autonomous.control: Power Platform admin center (environment, data policies, billing). Agent 365 can flag agents that have no owner.
watch: Agent flows started by an autonomous run consume credits at the standard rate too.

m365-graph.title: Copilot searches Microsoft 365 through Microsoft Graph
m365-graph.access: Only content the user can already open, found through the semantic index. Overshared files count as 'can open'.
m365-graph.control: SharePoint admin (Restricted Content Discovery as a stopgap, Restricted Access Control) and Purview (sensitivity labels, DLP for Copilot).
m365-graph.logs: Purview audit. DSPM for AI reports AI activity and oversharing.
watch: Copilot uses an encrypted file only if the user has both the VIEW and EXTRACT rights.

m365-payg-agent.title: A pay-as-you-go agent grounds the answer in SharePoint
m365-payg-agent.identity: The same employee. Results are trimmed to what they can open.
m365-payg-agent.access: For users without a Copilot license, tenant content arrives only through metered agents like this one.
m365-payg-agent.cost: Each answer is a generative answer (2 credits) plus tenant graph grounding (10).
m365-payg-agent.control: Microsoft 365 admin center: the pay-as-you-go billing policy and which agents these users get.
watch: Agents grounded only in instructions and public websites are free for these users. Grounding on SharePoint is what turns on the meter.

web-grounding.title: Copilot answers from the public web
web-grounding.identity: The same employee. Web search queries go out; no organizational data is involved.
web-grounding.cost: Included for licensed users and for Copilot Chat users alike.
web-grounding.logs: Purview audit records the Copilot interaction.

studio-sharepoint.title: The agent answers from SharePoint knowledge
studio-sharepoint.identity: Calls are made on behalf of the signed-in user.
studio-sharepoint.access: Trimmed to what that user can open. Files uploaded into the agent sit in Dataverse and aren't trimmed, so anyone who can use the agent can get answers from them.
studio-sharepoint.cost: A generative answer (2 credits) plus tenant graph grounding (10) when it searches Microsoft 365.
studio-sharepoint.control: SharePoint permissions are the real boundary; Power Platform data policies govern the agent.
watch: Tenant graph grounding needs generative orchestration, 'Authenticate with Microsoft' and at least one Copilot license in the tenant.

studio-public-web.title: The agent answers from public website content
studio-public-web.access: Public content only, so per-user permissions don't matter.
studio-public-web.cost: A generative answer (2 credits) per reply.
studio-public-web.control: The agent's knowledge settings. With 'Allow ungrounded responses' off, answers without a source are blocked.

genie-plugin.title: The Azure Databricks Genie plugin calls Genie One
genie-plugin.identity: Each user installs the plugin and signs in with Entra ID, so Genie sees the same person.
genie-plugin.access: Answers come from workspace-level Genie One. The plugin has no VNet support, and each user's connection is their own.
genie-plugin.cost: The plugin needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot license; chatting with it is part of that user's Copilot experience. Genie's side bills on Databricks.
genie-plugin.control: Databricks workspace admins enable Genie One; users install the plugin themselves.
genie-plugin.logs: Purview audit records the Copilot interaction.
watch: Unlicensed users can't use the plugin. The Genie app for Teams is their path.

genie-teams-app.title: The Databricks Genie app for Teams calls Genie
genie-teams-app.identity: Each request runs as the user who asked.
genie-teams-app.access: Answers come from Genie One, or from a Genie Agent an admin pinned. Copilot-licensed users can also @-mention the app in Copilot.
genie-teams-app.cost: No Copilot license needed. Genie's side bills on Databricks.
genie-teams-app.control: Entra (tenant-wide consent for the Azure Databricks app) and the Microsoft 365 admin who installs it. Private Link workspaces need an ingress rule.
genie-teams-app.logs: The app's central service runs in East US 2 and stores only the tenant-to-workspace mapping.
watch: Copilot doesn't route questions to Genie on its own: users have to @-mention it.

studio-genie-tool.title: The agent calls the Azure Databricks Genie tool

identity.user: Per-user OAuth: the call carries the signed-in user's identity. That needs Power Platform and Databricks in the same Entra tenant.
identity.sp: One service principal makes every call, whoever is asking.

studio-genie-tool.access: The tool reaches one Genie Agent, by ID, through Databricks' managed MCP server.
studio-genie-tool.cost: Each Genie call is an agent action (5 credits), and the reply is a generative answer (2).
studio-genie-tool.control: A Databricks workspace admin enables the Managed MCP Servers preview. The agent needs generative orchestration, and Power Platform data policies govern the connector.
studio-genie-tool.logs: Purview audit records maker activity; Databricks logs the Genie side.

sp: Cross-tenant setups have to use a service principal, which flattens per-user permissions.

genie-cowork.title: Cowork calls Genie One through the Genie plugin
genie-cowork.identity: The employee, signed in with Entra ID.
genie-cowork.access: Genie One answers with progress updates, visuals and citations, using the user's own permissions.
genie-cowork.cost: Cowork's model responses and tool calls consume Copilot Credits. Genie's AI and compute bill on the Databricks side.
genie-cowork.control: Spending policies for Cowork, and Databricks workspace settings for Genie One.
genie-cowork.logs: Copilot Cost Management for the credits; Databricks for the query.

genie-query-user.title: Genie writes SQL and runs it on a SQL warehouse
genie-query-user.access: Unity Catalog checks that user's grants, row filters and column masks on every query. The data stays where it is.
genie-query-user.cost: Genie's AI counts against the user's monthly allowance (150 DBUs, about $10) and is free for users through January 31, 2027. Warehouse compute is billed in DBUs either way.
genie-query-user.control: Databricks: Unity Catalog grants, consumer access, and Unity Gateway budgets, which cover Genie.
genie-query-user.logs: Databricks audit logs and query history, both in system tables.
watch: Genie One artifacts store a snapshot of their data, so sharing an artifact shares the data.

genie-query-sp.title: Genie writes SQL and runs it on a SQL warehouse
genie-query-sp.identity: The service principal, for every user.
genie-query-sp.access: Row filters and column masks are evaluated for the service principal, so everyone sees the same rows. Grant it only what every user may see.
genie-query-sp.cost: Service principals don't get the free allowance: Genie's AI bills at standard pay-as-you-go from the first question, plus warehouse compute.
genie-query-sp.control: Databricks: Unity Catalog grants on the service principal, and Unity Gateway budgets.
genie-query-sp.logs: Databricks audit logs and query history, which show the service principal, not the person who asked.

fabric-agent-copilot.title: A published Fabric data agent answers in Copilot or Teams
fabric-agent-copilot.identity: The asking user, signed in to Fabric and Copilot in the same tenant.
fabric-agent-copilot.access: Read-only queries as that user, so semantic model RLS and CLS still apply. Results are capped at 25 rows by 25 columns.
fabric-agent-copilot.cost: Each user needs a Microsoft Copilot license or an Office 365 commercial subscription. The agent's work consumes Fabric capacity, not Copilot Credits.
fabric-agent-copilot.control: Fabric admin portal: Copilot and AI tenant settings, including cross-geo processing, plus access to the agent and each of its sources.
fabric-agent-copilot.logs: The Capacity Metrics app shows consumption; Purview audit covers Fabric activity.
watch: Microsoft warns that responses may be processed outside Fabric's compliance boundary or region.

studio-fabric-connected.title: The agent hands the question to a connected Fabric data agent
studio-fabric-connected.access: As if the user called the data agent directly: read-only, with their own permissions.
studio-fabric-connected.cost: This simulator counts the hand-off as one agent action (5 credits), like a tool call, plus the generative answer (2). The data agent's tokens bill to Fabric capacity.
studio-fabric-connected.control: Power Platform admin center for the agent; Fabric tenant settings for the data agent.
studio-fabric-connected.logs: Purview audit for the agent; the Capacity Metrics app for Fabric.
watch: Microsoft's multi-agent page says Fabric data agents don't work when the main agent is deployed to Microsoft 365 Copilot, and these connections are in preview. Check the channel first.

fabric-query.title: The data agent runs on Fabric capacity
fabric-query.access: Up to five sources (lakehouses, warehouses, KQL databases, semantic models, ontologies), read-only, English only, no unstructured files.
fabric-query.cost: Tokens convert to capacity: 100 CU-seconds per 1,000 input tokens and 400 per 1,000 output tokens, smoothed as background work.
fabric-query.control: The capacity holding the content pays, unless the user is assigned a Fabric Copilot capacity. It needs paid F2+ or P1+; trial capacities don't support it.
fabric-query.logs: The Capacity Metrics app (14 days, about 10 to 15 minutes behind).

cowork-work.title: Cowork plans and runs the task

access.web: Browser tasks reach the public web for the user.
access.default: Work IQ grounds it in the user's Microsoft 365 content, within the user's permissions.

cowork-work.cost: Model responses, tool calls and browser tasks all consume Copilot Credits.
cowork-work.control: Spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
cowork-work.logs: Copilot Cost Management reports credit usage.

autonomous-sharepoint.title: The agent reads SharePoint through its connection
autonomous-sharepoint.identity: The account behind the connection, not any employee.
autonomous-sharepoint.access: Everything that account can open is in reach, so scope the account tightly.
autonomous-sharepoint.cost: Each connector call is an agent action (5 credits), and a generated reply adds a generative answer (2).
autonomous-sharepoint.control: Power Platform data policies for the connector, and SharePoint permissions on the connection's account.

external-not-in-tenant.title: External customers can't use your tenant's Copilot, Teams apps or Cowork
external-not-in-tenant.why: They have no account in your Entra tenant, and all three sign users in with Entra ID. Reach customers with a Copilot Studio agent published to a website instead.
external-not-in-tenant.insteadLabel: Try a Copilot Studio agent on a website

cowork-needs-license.title: Cowork needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot license
cowork-needs-license.why: Cowork runs on top of the Copilot license, plus usage-based billing that a spending policy grants. Users without the license can't start Cowork tasks.
cowork-needs-license.insteadLabel: Try it as a licensed employee

genie-plugin-needs-license.title: The Genie plugin needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot license
genie-plugin-needs-license.why: The Azure Databricks Genie plugin works in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Cowork for licensed users. For users without a license, Databricks points to the Genie app for Teams.
genie-plugin-needs-license.insteadLabel: Try the Genie app for Teams

website-sharepoint.title: A website agent can't answer from SharePoint with the default sign-in
website-sharepoint.why: SharePoint knowledge needs users to sign in, and 'Authenticate with Microsoft' works in Teams, Power Apps and Microsoft Copilot, not on a public website. External customers can't sign in to your tenant at all.
website-sharepoint.insteadLabel: Publish the agent in Teams or Copilot instead
website-sharepoint.insteadExternalLabel: Ground the website agent on public content instead

fabric-needs-user.title: Fabric data agents need a signed-in user
fabric-needs-user.why: A data agent queries read-only with the asking user's identity, and that user has to sign in to Fabric and Copilot in the same tenant. A website visitor or an event-triggered run has no such user.
fabric-needs-user.insteadLabel: Compare with Genie through a service principal

cowork-fabric.title: No documented path from Cowork to a Fabric data agent
cowork-fabric.why: This simulator only follows documented paths. Cowork reaches Databricks through the Genie plugin; for Fabric, a published data agent answers in Copilot Chat or Teams.
cowork-fabric.insteadLabel: Ask the data agent in Copilot Chat instead
